in_text_mentions: vaginal introitus due to the fusion of the labia majora. Her primary complaints included dysuria and intermittent urine leakage. The constant moisture in the vulvar region caused by dribbling urine resulted in irritation, leading to the progression of the labial adhesion to its complete form. Upon clinical examination, there was only a small opening of approximately 5 mm at the posterior fourchette, sufficient for urine to escape drop by drop. Additionally, the anterior fusion was accompanied by the partial disappearance of the clitoral hood, which is the skin covering the clitoris (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: Labial adhesions are observed at the 0 and 6 o'clock positions at the vaginal introitus

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of the vulva showing labial adhesions at the 0 and 6 o'clock positions with vaginal introitus stenosis, consistent with the configured disease labial adhesions due to vulvovaginal lichen planus. Mucosal erythema and lace-like hyperkeratosis are also present. B: H&E skin biopsy from the labia showing hyperkeratosis, atrophic epidermis, band-like chronic inflammatory infiltrate, and Civatte bodies, consistent with lichen planus, the underlying cause of the labial adhesions in this article.

(b) Skin biopsy at the time of labia detachment showing hyperkeratosis, mildly atrophic epidermis with flattened basal keratinocytes, and a band‐like infiltrate of chronic inflammatory cells involving the subepidermal dermis. Civatte bodies are also observed in the suprabasal layers (Hematoxylin and eosin; total magnification ×100).

plate_findings.evidence: Markedly edematous and protruding labia majora with complete midline fusion

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph directly demonstrating complete midline labial fusion with edematous labia majora in a patient with labial adhesions; the caption and in-text explicitly describe the complete midline fusion covering the introitus. [raw subtype: complete labial fusion] B: Transperineal ultrasound from the same patient demonstrating hydrocolpos and distended vestibule as direct anatomical consequences of complete labial fusion; the in-text explicitly links the ultrasound findings to the labial fusion. panels.rationale: Real-patient abdominal/pelvic ultrasound annotated 'bladder' and 'urocolpos', depicting urine retention in the vagina secondary to complete labial fusion - the bladder outlet obstruction complication described in this labial adhesions case report. The adhesion itself is not directly visualized (the vocabulary's mucosa-based findings cannot be assessed on ultrasound), so attribution relies on the caption and in-text description; confidence is therefore moderate.
panels.attribution_text: Tîrnovanu et al. Bladder Outlet Obstruction Due to Recurrent Complete Labial Fusion in Postmenopausal Woman-Case Report.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland) 2024. doi:10.3390/diagnostics14232659. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound at first admission for labial fusion.
in_text_mentions: t infection with Escherichia coli was identified via bladder catheterization. The anatomical region affected by the synechia had formed a pocket, predisposing it to urine retention and microbial proliferation. In the middle third of the labial coalescence, a 5 mm membrane allowed for urine to exit during abdominal compression. An abdominal ultrasound examination revealed urine in both the bladder and the urocolpos (Figure 2), along with bilateral hydronephrosis classified as grade I. We successfully inserted a urinary catheter into the vagina, which resulted in the discharge of 1.5 L of urine.

in_text_mentions: A 91-year-old postmenopausal woman with a prior history of two labial-adhesion separations suffered from recurrent urinary-tract infections. Genital examination revealed labial adhesions obscuring the external urethral orifice (Figure 1). Urinalysis showed pyuria, and her urine culture was positive for Escherichia coli (2 × 105/mL). We prescribed topical estrogen ointment, but after 10 days the patient complained of paresthesia in her left breast. As the treatment was not having any effect at that point, we discontinued it and planned for surgical intervention under local anesthesia.

in_text_mentions: General and systemic examination revealed no abnormalities. The patient had age-appropriate secondary sexual characteristics. On local examination of the external genitalia, the labia majora appeared normal. The labia minora were densely adherent across the midline, resulting in near-complete obliteration of the vaginal introitus. There were no signs of active inflammation, ulceration, or skin discoloration, as shown in Figure 1.
